jobDescription: Brackenhurst Logistics runs contract warehouses for retail and healthcare clients. The Warehouse Systems Coordinator configures the warehouse management system, writes work instructions, trains operatives on handheld scanning, arranges devices with IT and leads system changes into live operation on working shifts, staying on the floor to support users after cut-over. Each site runs two or three shifts a day, healthcare clients require batch and expiry capture on every scan, and the coordinator works with site general managers, client account teams and the IT service desk. System changes follow a cut-over plan agreed with the site general manager and are rehearsed in a training instance first.
requirements: Configures putaway and picking rules in a warehouse management system.
Writes work instructions for warehouse system processes.
Has taken a warehouse system change into live operation on a working shift and supported users after cut-over.
Trains warehouse operatives on handheld scanning.

evidence.text: Inventory Systems Assistant, Fellgate Distribution, November 2022 to August 2024: set up putaway and pick-face rules in the WMS training instance for a new handheld scanning workflow, covering three temperature zones and two pick-face sizes.
Wrote 14 illustrated work instructions for receiving, putaway and replenishment on the handheld scanners, each with photographs of the scanner screens and the exception steps.
Trained 40 operatives over two weeks of half-day sessions in the training warehouse, a mocked-up aisle stocked with dummy cartons, keeping attendance records for each session.
Registered 60 handheld scanners with the IT service desk, checking each device's enrolment and app version before issue, and kept the device register up to date.
Handheld scanning rollout at the Daventry site: per the client's account director, the new workflow 'has been live on every shift since the spring', with no paper pick lists left.

Work sample: the report from two rehearsal nights in the training instance, listing the scripted scenarios, the scan errors found and the fixes applied, with a cover note listing the open actions to close before a cut-over date could be set, including a missing label printer and two unresolved scan errors.

HR verification note: employment at Fellgate Distribution from November 2022 to August 2024 was confirmed against the payroll record that the former employer supplied, together with the job title Inventory Systems Assistant.
Reference check summary: Fellgate's site training manager confirmed in writing that the candidate wrote the scanner work instructions and delivered the operative training in the training warehouse.

propositions.text: The candidate set up putaway and pick-face rules in the WMS training instance for the handheld scanning workflow.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the configuration in the training instance.

propositions.text: The candidate took the handheld scanning workflow live on every shift at the Daventry site and supported users after cut-over.
propositions.rationale: The go-live statement is quoted from the client's account director and does not say what the candidate did; the rehearsal report and training sources keep the work in the training instance with cut-over actions still open. The deployment rule does not allow rehearsal or training work to be described as live operation without a source that says it went live.

propositions.text: The candidate trained 40 operatives over two weeks in a mocked-up training warehouse.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the training and the reference check confirms it in writing.

gold.expectedGap: The documented work is configuration, rehearsal and training in the training instance; a live cut-over on a working shift and post-cut-over support are not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the training-instance configuration, the rehearsals, the work instructions and the training; record the go-live remark as the client's account director's words, not as the candidate's cut-over.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the scanning workflow was cut over at Daventry while the candidate was there, who led the cut-over and what floor support the candidate gave afterwards.
